title: Lifecycle of an appropriation

activities.name: Agency formulation
activities.example: The agency identifies a flood-damaged bridge on a federal road and requests $10 million for a bridge-repair program. The request explains the need, proposed work, and estimated cost.

activities.name: OMB review and passback
activities.example: OMB reviews the $10 million request and asks the agency to revise its repair priorities and delivery schedule. The agency submits an updated request; this is still planning for proposed funding.
activities.example_document: OMB passback and versioned agency response

activities.name: President’s budget
activities.example: The President’s budget proposes $10 million for the bridge-repair program and is transmitted to Congress. The proposal does not itself provide spending authority.

activities.name: Congressional consideration
activities.example: Enacted legislation provides $10 million for the bridge-repair program. The agency records the legal reference, purpose, amount, and availability period before beginning execution.

activities.name: Apportionment
activities.example: OMB approves a $2.5 million apportionment for the period, subject to its conditions. The approved schedule links this limit to the original $10 million appropriation.

activities.name: Allotment
activities.example: The agency allots $1 million of the apportioned $2.5 million to the district responsible for the bridge. The district’s allotment and its restrictions are recorded in the funds-control system.

activities.name: Obligations and commitments
activities.example: After the necessary reviews, the district signs a $750,000 bridge-repair contract. The agency records this obligation against the $1 million allotment.

activities.name: Disbursements
activities.example: Engineers accept the first stage of work, and an approved invoice results in a $500,000 payment through Treasury. The contract still has $250,000 obligated but unpaid.
activities.example_document: Acceptance record, approved invoice, and payment receipt

activities.name: Closeout and audit
activities.example: Later, after the remaining work and final $250,000 payment are complete, staff reconcile the contract and retain its audit trail. The appropriation account closes under its own availability and cancellation rules.

timeframe: Follow one funding request through enactment, execution, and closeout. Appropriations have different availability periods, and their lifecycle can span multiple fiscal years.
